name: calc-evolution
description: Three checkpoints of a tiny TypeScript calculator library: add/negate at T0, subtract introduced at T1, negate removed and VERSION bumped to 2.0.0 at T2. The ledger is a complete census of every material fact about the library at each checkpoint (identity, layout, module locations, exports, typing, purity, docs, per-function behavior, version value), not a list of deltas, so precision is measured against everything true rather than a thin sample. Exercises discovery, retention, complete forgetting, and changed-knowledge correction.

versions.statement: The repository is `calc`, a tiny calculator (arithmetic) library.
The source describes calc as a tiny arithmetic library used as a KEB smoke-test fixture.
The complete repository contains exactly three tracked files: `README.md`, `src/calc.ts`, and `src/version.ts`.
The repository root contains `README.md` and the `src/` directory.
The complete TypeScript source surface consists of exactly two files under `src/`: `src/calc.ts` and `src/version.ts`.
The repository contains no test files or test directory.
The repository contains no package manifest or `package.json` file.
The TypeScript source imports no modules.
The repository has no index, barrel, or package entrypoint module.
Every runtime declaration in the TypeScript source is exported; there are no private helper functions, classes, types, interfaces, or internal constants.
The complete public surface has exactly three named exports: the functions `add` and `negate`, plus the `VERSION` constant.
The complete public surface has exactly four named exports: the functions `add`, `negate`, and `subtract`, plus the `VERSION` constant.
The complete public surface has exactly three named exports: the functions `add` and `subtract`, plus the `VERSION` constant; `negate` is no longer exported or present.
The library is written in TypeScript and every public value (the functions and the VERSION constant) is an ES module named export, imported individually; there is no default export.
All source code lives under a top-level `src/` directory.
The arithmetic functions are defined in the module `src/calc.ts`.
`src/calc.ts` begins with a module-level JSDoc comment describing the file as a tiny arithmetic library used as a KEB smoke-test fixture and stating its purity constraints.
The library's version string is defined in its own module, `src/version.ts`, separate from the arithmetic code.
`src/version.ts` contains only a JSDoc-documented named string constant `VERSION`, described as the library's released version string.
A root `README.md` documents the current version and the public API, listing each function as a bullet under an `## API` heading.
`README.md` starts with the H1 heading `calc`.
The README explicitly states that all functions are pure, perform no input validation, rounding, or I/O, and are TypeScript ES module named exports.
Every exported function carries a JSDoc comment documenting each parameter and its return value.
Every exported function is pure: it performs no input validation, no rounding, and no I/O, and returns a value computed only from its arguments.
Every arithmetic function takes and returns TypeScript `number` values.
`add` has the TypeScript signature `add(a: number, b: number): number`.
`negate` has the TypeScript signature `negate(x: number): number`.
`subtract` has the TypeScript signature `subtract(a: number, b: number): number`.
`add(a, b)` returns the sum of its two number arguments.
The complete implementation of `add` is `return a + b;`; it contains no branches, helper calls, or other operations.
`negate(x)` returns the additive inverse (negation) of its single argument.
The complete implementation of `negate` is `return -x;`; it contains no branches, helper calls, or other operations.
`subtract(a, b)` returns the difference of its two arguments, the first minus the second (`a - b`).
The complete implementation of `subtract` is `return a - b;`; it contains no branches, helper calls, or other operations.
At version 1.0.0 the README API list documents exactly `add(a, b)` and `negate(x)`.
After subtract is introduced, the README API list documents exactly `add(a, b)`, `negate(x)`, and `subtract(a, b)`.
At version 2.0.0 the README API list documents exactly `add(a, b)` and `subtract(a, b)`; it no longer lists `negate(x)`.
The repository root has no entries other than `README.md` and `src/`.

The README contains the exact Markdown line: `The exported `VERSION` constant is `"2.0.0"`.`
The README has exactly one H2 heading, `API`.

The `src/calc.ts` module docblock states exactly: `A tiny arithmetic library used as a KEB smoke-test fixture. Every function is a pure function of its arguments: no input validation, no rounding, and no I/O.`
`src/version.ts` contains exactly `export const VERSION = "1.0.0";` after its JSDoc comment.
`src/version.ts` contains exactly `export const VERSION = "2.0.0";` after its JSDoc comment.
The JSDoc for `add` identifies `a` as the left operand, `b` as the right operand, and the return value as the sum of `a` and `b`.
The JSDoc for `negate` identifies `x` as the value to negate and the return value as the additive inverse of `x`.
The JSDoc for `subtract` identifies `a` as the number to subtract from, `b` as the number to subtract, and the return value as the difference `a - b`.

The arithmetic functions use JavaScript's native `number` operators directly, so they preserve native NaN, infinity, signed-zero, and floating-point behavior without special cases or precision correction.
`add(NaN, 1)` is NaN; `add(Infinity, 1)` is Infinity; `add(Infinity, -Infinity)` is NaN; `add(-Infinity, 1)` is -Infinity; `add(-0, 0)` is 0; and `add(0.1, 0.2)` is 0.30000000000000004.
`negate(NaN)` is NaN; `negate(Infinity)` is -Infinity; `negate(-Infinity)` is Infinity; `negate(0)` is -0; `negate(-0)` is 0; and `negate(0.1)` is -0.1.

`subtract(NaN, 1)` is NaN; `subtract(Infinity, 1)` is Infinity; `subtract(Infinity, Infinity)` is NaN; `subtract(-Infinity, 1)` is -Infinity; `subtract(0, 0)` is 0; `subtract(-0, 0)` is -0; and `subtract(0.3, 0.1)` is 0.19999999999999998.
The exported VERSION constant is the string "1.0.0", and the README states the library version is 1.0.0.
The exported VERSION constant is the string "2.0.0", and the README states the library version is 2.0.0.
